questions.question: What is the difference between `groupby().agg()` and `groupby().transform()`?
options: `agg()` returns the same number of rows as the input; `transform()` reduces to one row per group
`agg()` reduces to one row per group; `transform()` returns the same number of rows as the input
They are identical in behavior
`transform()` only works with numeric columns
questions.explanation: `agg()` produces a summary with one row per group (reducing). `transform()` broadcasts the aggregated result back to every original row, keeping the same shape. Use `transform` when you want to add a group-level summary as a new column.

questions.question: What does `pd.merge(orders, customers, on='customer_id', how='left')` do?
options: Returns only rows where `customer_id` exists in both DataFrames
Returns all rows from `orders`, with matching columns from `customers` (NaN if no match)
Returns all rows from `customers`, with matching columns from `orders`
Returns all rows from both DataFrames including unmatched rows
questions.explanation: A left join keeps all rows from the left DataFrame (`orders`) and fills in matching data from the right (`customers`). If a `customer_id` in orders has no match in customers, the customer columns will be NaN.

questions.question: What does `pd.pivot_table(df, values='revenue', index='region', columns='month', aggfunc='sum')` produce?
options: A sorted DataFrame ordered by revenue
A 2D table with regions as rows, months as columns, and summed revenue as values
A single column of total revenue per region
A long-format table with one row per region-month combination
questions.explanation: A pivot table reshapes data from long to wide format. `index` becomes the row labels, `columns` becomes the column headers, and `values` are aggregated by `aggfunc`. The result is a cross-tabulation—similar to a spreadsheet pivot table.

questions.question: Given a DatetimeIndex, what does `.resample('M').sum()` do?
options: Sums every M rows (every 1000 rows)
Groups data by month and sums values within each month
Resets the index to monthly integers
Multiplies all values by M (a constant)
questions.explanation: `resample()` groups time-series data into regular time intervals. `'M'` means month-end frequency. `.sum()` then aggregates all rows in each month. This is the time-series equivalent of `groupby()`.

questions.question: Which method fills missing values in a column with the column's mean?
options: `df['col'].replace(NaN, df['col'].mean())`
`df['col'].fillna(df['col'].mean())`
`df['col'].dropna(fill=df['col'].mean())`
`df['col'].impute('mean')`
questions.explanation: `fillna()` replaces NaN values with the specified value. Passing `df['col'].mean()` as the argument fills each NaN with the column average. Other common options include `fillna(0)`, `fillna(method='ffill')` (forward fill), and `fillna(method='bfill')` (backward fill).
